in_sanskrit.name: माधवी
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The one who is 'maadh' (intoxicated) with the beauty of the Lord, or the one who is 'madh' (passionate) towards the Lord. Derived from the Sanskrit word 'maadhava' meaning 'Lord of the universe', often used to refer to Lord Krishna or Vishnu.

in_hindi.name: माधवी
in_hindi.long_meaning: The one with beautiful limbs, or the one with a beautiful appearance. In Hindu mythology, Maadhavi is also considered a form of Goddess Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth and prosperity.

in_tamil.name: மாதவி
in_tamil.long_meaning: The one with a charming face, or the one with a beautiful smile. In Hindu mythology, Maadhavi is also considered a form of Goddess Meenakshi, the goddess of Madurai.

in_telugu.name: మాధవీ
in_telugu.long_meaning: The one who is the consort of Lord Mahadeva, or the one who is the goddess of the Kailasa mountain. In Hindu mythology, Maadhavi is also considered a form of Goddess Parvathi, the consort of Lord Shiva.

in_marathi.name: Maadhavi
in_marathi.meaning: हिंदू नाव म्हणजे Goddess of wealth
in_marathi.long_meaning: Maadhavi हे एक हिंदू नाव आहे जे भारतीय संस्कृतीत खोल आध्यात्मिक महत्त्व ठेवते। The name Maadhavi is derived from the Sanskrit language and is the name of the goddess of wealth and prosperity in Hindu mythology. She is often depicted holding a lotus in her hands and is believed to bestow her blessings upon her devotees for abundance and prosperity.
